speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is said that if the country's economy is the lifeline of our country and infrastructure is the skeleton of our country, then arts and culture must be the soul of our country.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is the arts and cultures that define us.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Through arts and culture, we forged a national identity that unites all of us as one people, one nation, one Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: As a multicultural and multi-religious society, we have done well to respect and appreciate one another's cultural differences to practise acceptance and compromise.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Yet, the threat of social division and fragmentation can never be completely eliminated.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Even as we observe the civil conflicts occurring around the world from afar, we cannot take our peace for granted and assume these problems will not happen in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: This is especially so when there are strong external influences that can disrupt our social cohesion.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: There have been Singaporeans who were self-radicalised to embrace extremist beliefs and even wanted to head overseas to support armed conflict or conduct attacks here.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Fortunately, in some cases, family and loved ones had stepped in to intervene.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Meanwhile, concerns of social divide were sparked following a study that revealed a clear divide among social classes in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Rising living costs and other challenges give rise to problems that may estrange certain groups of people.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The cumulative effect of segregation and dissatisfaction can result in an "us versus them" mentality, which will lead to larger cracks over time.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Active participation from Singaporeans in these areas have helped to foster a stronger sense of unity and pride.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We must continue to encourage greater vibrancy and participation in these sectors to create shared experiences, ensuring that our society remains resilient and cohesive.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Government is planning to do more at the school level, but how about the older youths who are more inclined to feel disillusioned?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We want a nation that all Singaporeans are proud to call home.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How do we measure the strength of our social fabric?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What more can we do to strengthen the Singapore spirit and identity?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   In order to help children from disadvantaged families, it is important that we give them a good foundation and provide them with quality preschool education.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: By virtue of their family's social and financial situation, some of the children from low-income families may not have the opportunity to grow up in a learning environment to prepare them for primary school education.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are a few occasions during house visits in my neighbourhood where I will meet children aged four to seven who did not attend preschool, and there are those who do, but for certain reasons, are unable to read at Primary 1.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When they were asked to attend and learn to read, some of them manage to excel in primary school.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They are actually quite smart but they need some help and close guidance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to make a concerted effort to help these children, including getting the support of parents, teachers and allied education professionals, to get the children involved and engaged in activities that can enrich their young minds to be interested in learning, asking questions, and wanting to listen and understand.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I agree that childhood is not a rat race to get the child to read, write and count quickly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But it is important that we lay the foundation so that when the time comes, they are on the right track.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Children learn best in an environment that provides high-quality human interactions and learning from the same group of teachers over a long period so that they are at ease.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Hence, I note that the Ministry of Education (MOE) has already recognised that the early years are crucial for a child’s holistic development.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Ministry’s view is that quality preschool education would provide the child with opportunities to gain self-confidence, learn social skills and develop learning dispositions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I hope that, as a community, we can work together to ensure that these children get what they truly need.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Access to education, regardless of family background, ensures that the entire community can progress together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With this, the next generation would have greater opportunities to excel.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Our madrasahs are key institutions that produce our future leaders and religious teachers to guide and provide advice to the Malay/Muslim community on religious matters in a context that is suited to our multiracial and multi-religious society and our customs.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Several of our madrasahs also have long histories and legacies that can reflect the development of Islam and the Malay/Muslim community here.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I understand that Madrasah Wak Tanjong, which has a very long history and legacy, is due for its lease renewal and this involves very high costs.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   It is important to ensure that madrasah students and teachers in Singapore receive support and opportunities to upgrade themselves in order to grow a strong socio-religious sector.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Our asatizahs play an important role in providing the community with sound religious leadership and guidance that are suited to Singapore’s context and modern realities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Madrasahs play an important role in developing future generations of asatizahs with a strong foundation in both religious and secular subjects.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: He said that the new campus would be equipped with the latest technological infrastructure and facilities to serve its students and the community.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Last year, when the issue of the Elected Presidency caught our attention, there was a discussion on the issue of Malayness.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This discussion did not take place among Malay Singaporeans only but also received significant attention from Singaporeans in general.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The question being hotly debated was how a person is recognised as a Malay or who can be called a Malay.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Many questions were asked, views being brought forward and many examples were also highlighted.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In short, there was a robust and lively discussion, just to seek a real answer on the issue of Malayness.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand, and I believe the other Malay Members of Parliament (MPs) in this Chamber do, too, why this issue of identity cropped up.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, in order to explain this matter clearly, I would like to give an illustration or example.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This individual tried to explain that he speaks Malay at home and he leads his life as a Malay; he eats asam pedas, wears baju kurung during Hari Raya and so on.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: But the reply he got was "Sorry, your identity card shows that your race is Indian." Time passed, and the same individual obtained his degree, started work and got married.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He then decided to serve the people through politics.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He wanted to contest in the General Elections.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: During the General Elections, this individual then decided to contest in a Group Representation Constituency (GRC) as the Malay minority candidate.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: He submitted an application form to the Elections Department to obtain the Certificate of the Malay Community Committee, but he is not that confident whether his application will be accepted or otherwise, since his identity card showed that his race is Indian.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, he does not feel comfortable to apply as an Indian minority candidate since he does not possess any characteristics as someone who is Indian.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Many of these organisations often tapped on the same pool of donors and this limits their fundraising effort to a certain extent.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, the matching grant that the Government provides helps ease the load for many of them.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: When this happens, it means these organisations have to work even harder to raise their own funds to make up for the shortfall from the deduction of the dollar-for-dollar matching grant.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This can also distract the organisations from focusing on what they should be doing best, that is, providing programmes for community benefit rather than spending time to look for funds.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: It may be made worse when a matching fund can become the end game of these organisations.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: During times of economic downturn, raising funds becomes an even bigger problem when people are less likely to donate and yet, at the same time, the demand for the services provided by these organisations increase.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: So, this, essentially, means the organisations may be in a situation where the number of clients in need increase and yet their funds decrease.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This may end up in organisations having to scale down their operations or the extent of their services, causing them to be unable to serve those in need effectively.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Ultimately, a reduction in funds leads not only to operational challenges for the organisations but may also exacerbate challenges for Singaporeans in need as their needs are left unserved.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, when a matching grant gets re-allocated or reduced, the criteria applied to determine how this is done are also not made clear.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Clear criteria will help organisations to better understand their qualification.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This will help Government funds to be fully utilised to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, it will also encourage VWOs and SHGs currently not eligible for matching grants to start taking measures in order to meet those criteria.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: First, the integrity and maturity of the VWOs and SHGs; and second, the outreach the SHGs and VWOs had achieved in previous years.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: These criteria can help to determine which organisations can qualify for the matching grant and what the cap for the grant could be.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Integrity and maturity of VWOs and SHGs would be a useful measure of whether they would be able to utilise the funds appropriately.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: VWOs or SHGs that have long been established and have a good track record in terms of governance and the programmes and services provided should be accorded a higher cap in the grant.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, an organisation that has a good record of outreach historically could be given even a higher cap.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: By offering tiered grants, it will encourage our organisations, both SHGs and VWOs, to improve their processes, governance and standards as well as quality of programmes and services, leading to a more vibrant VWO sector which can only benefit more Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Eventually, it is hoped that more beneficiaries can be reached and served and this can only be a positive development for Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: They offer various forms of assistance and social service and are instrumental in uplifting certain parameters in our communities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Every year, these organisations will disburse financial and educational assistance as well as bursaries and other forms of help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There, however, exist some grey areas and overlap.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is important for us to know and understand this because we want to know how many fall through the cracks yearly and also how we can work together to assist these people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Detailed analysis of the causation and other parameters will be helpful to understand as we, together, vow to strengthen our community outreach.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many officers from our Malay/Muslim organisations have been trained under this development fund and how have they benefited from this?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What other measures should the Government take to help these organisations enhance their efforts and skills in assisting the community?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Do these Malay/Muslim organisations also focus on training their younger leaders to take over each organisations' leadership?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, the Malay Youth Literary Association (4PM) specialises in youth-related efforts and outreach, while the Young Women Muslim Association of Singapore (PPIS) specialises in helping women and children.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This specialisation is important so that each Malay/Muslim organisation can sharpen their capabilities and skills and allocate all their manpower and funds towards helping specific groups.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This can also prevent duplication of efforts, energy and skills, and ensure a more efficient allocation of manpower and funds.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to call upon our Malay/Muslim organisations to spread their wings so that they can offer their assistance and expertise beyond the Malay community and, in fact, to all Singaporeans, in areas like eldercare, the disabled or those with special needs, early childhood education, as well as entrepreneurship.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One example is having one of our Malay/Muslim organisations build an eldercare centre, regardless of their race or religion.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our Malay/Muslim organisations should also be able to support entrepreneurship in various areas through skills development programmes or through social assistance networks and business dealings for entrepreneurs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that there can be some flexibility on the part of the Government when the MMCDF funds are used for such efforts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   The family is an important unit in society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: To ensure that a community is strong and robust, the family unit must be strong and robust.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Therefore, it is important that we continue paying attention to efforts that build and preserve family ties.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Among efforts being done include conducting courses that are suitable for families, including couples who wish to marry or have just married, parents with young children, and so on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Over the years, we have seen many developments amongst our Malay/Muslim families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand that more are getting married and there are fewer marriages between couples under 21 years old.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We also see fewer cases of remarriages after a divorce.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Although there is a slight improvement, divorce rates appear stable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I feel that there is still room for us to continue helping couples and families in this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One specific effort being done is to monitor and provide guidance to young couples under 21 years old.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Can the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs provide the latest information on this matter?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Now, we are embarking on setting up an Islamic college.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Looking at the global trends and what is happening in the world today in terms of Islamic education, ideologies inculcation and the matters religious leaders and clerics have to grapple with, the time is right for us to undertake this and to grab the opportunity to make the positive impact that we have to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: This is a major undertaking and we must ensure we plan it right.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: It is not about imposing models from other countries to Singapore but more about customisation and implementing our own unique model for the College.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: We must also ensure that the College has engagement and outreach to the community and will prove beneficial to the future and potential students and educators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Have the relevant personnel planned the relevant engagements and focus group discussions with the local targeted stakeholders and what other progress has been made pertaining to the Singapore Islamic College?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: In addition, it can reduce the risk of our students being affected by any political instability in countries that offer Islamic education or studies, or the risk of them becoming victims of radical or extremist ideologies in some of these countries.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: What are MUIS' plans to ensure that this college can be as great as other Islamic universities with longer histories and are already well-known?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: What strategies or approaches have been planned to ensure that its educational programmes and subjects are relevant and global in nature and, at the same time, are based on Singapore's multiracial and multi-religious context, as well as the context of Southeast Asia?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: And how will this college's lecturers and academics be appointed and employed?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Do these lecturers and academics have to be trained solely as asatizahs, or perhaps should they also have more diverse backgrounds, experiences and training?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: (In Malay):   The threat of radicalism on our youths is a risk that comes from their exposure to undesirable elements on various social media platforms.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Our youths may not have or lack the maturity to differentiate between truth and falsehoods on social media.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: I feel that this is a good beginning and should be supported.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
text: (In Malay):   Since its formation in 1968, MUIS has touched the lives of many people, particularly Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, MUIS has played a key role in ensuring that the socio-religious lives of Muslims in Singapore are being looked after.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
text: As a former Council Member of MUIS, I have seen MUIS making every effort to stay relevant in this ever-changing world that we live in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
text: MUIS' efforts in building an excellent and inspiring Muslim community that is resilient, socially cohesive and thrives in a multi-religious society, secular state and globalised world are apt and commendable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
text: Could the Minister share some of the plans that MUIS is embarking on this year and MUIS' vision for the future?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: (In Malay):   During the dialogue sessions with our Malay/Muslim community, some issues that are frequently raised pertain to concerns about the ever-changing economy and efforts that individuals should make to keep updating their skills so that they stay relevant.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Many are aware about the importance of attending the right training courses so that they can upgrade themselves.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But some are worried whether they can still keep their jobs due to increasing competition.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some are unsure what they need to do to prepare for the new economy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Some also wish to know which sectors or industries will grow and should be given due attention.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Although I understand their concern, I am proud that there are an awareness and a desire to continue improving themselves.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Are there efforts to start early and engage students in order to inculcate awareness and skills about working in the new economy?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: What are the efforts done to keep encouraging students and PMETs to continue obtaining qualifications and upgrading themselves even if they have completed formal education in schools?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   We are all aware of the rapid digital transformation affecting all levels of society.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The most affected groups are those who are older and those who are not technologically or digitally savvy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, there are many opportunities available for these groups to help them acquire knowledge about the digital world.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, I was drawn to a newspaper article published not long ago about a group of hawkers who made use of digital payments.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The payment process became speedier and they do not have to bother looking for loose change for their customers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, in this regard, we understand that not everyone is able to swiftly embrace such changes due to several factors, for instance, lack of knowledge and unfamiliarity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, what is the progress of our community institutions in making use of digital solutions to enhance service levels?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The utilisation of data and digital solutions can enable businessmen and entrepreneurs to run their businesses better even with the lack of manpower.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What more can be done to encourage Malay/Muslim small and medium enterprises (SMEs) which have not undergone digital transformations to do so?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In his speech on the 20th anniversary of the CDCs last year, the Prime Minister identified the issue of worker upgrading as an urgent one.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is the position of the CDC as an intermediary necessary?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I clarify what is the nature of the relationship between an opposition MP and the Town Council of which he or she is an elected member on the one hand and the CDC on the other?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does it follow the approach taken by the People’s Association (PA) vis-à-vis Grassroots Advisers?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Appointing persons with such reputable civil and Public Service background and experience is very relevant and much more appropriate, as they are in a better position to explain Government policies and programmes to citizens, implementing social programmes, as well as helping the Government to connect better with the people.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Another positive reason for appointing such individuals is that it will help to eliminate or avoid any possibilities of (a) a conflict of interest; and (b) politicisation of the grassroots advisor position, as compared to the current practice of appointing the ruling party's defeated candidates and any other ruling political party members as the grassroots advisor.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Touching on the matter of politicisation and conflict of interest, I would like to seek answers from the Ministry whether there is, indeed, an element of politicisation and conflict of interest in the role of grassroots advisor in the following two scenarios.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I have cited these scenarios during the recent Public Sector (Governance) Bill to seek some clarification.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I was told by Minister Ong Ye Kung to direct the matter to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I submitted this cut under PMO but was redirected to MCCY.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Second scenario: a grassroots adviser conducts house visits accompanied by PA's grassroots leaders and staff of Statutory Boards, such as the Housing and Development Board (HDB), and inviting residents to attend his Meet-the-People session (MPS) if residents require him to appeal on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Nonetheless, the MPS session is held in a political party branch office by the grassroots advisor who writes referral or appeal letters using a political party's letterhead and signs off as the party branch chairman of a political party.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We strived hard to forge a better life and household incomes grew.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The community – from mothers and fathers to Cikgu in every classroom – put great emphasis on education as never before, and significant progress was made.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our community also emphasised mutual help and cooperation, especially in times of need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The spirit of gotong-royong was the driving force behind our community's setting up of Singapore's first Self-Help Group in 1982 to uplift education outcomes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our community also work hand-in-hand with our Government to build the legal and institutional foundations of our socio-religious life through AMLA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are in the midst of another economic transformation, brought about by a digital revolution no less fundamental than the Industrial Revolution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must prepare our industries and workers for the future economy, and we must make sure no one is left behind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also face an ongoing threat to our faith.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The spread of extremist ideologies abetted by social media and the acts of terror by the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS) have set Muslims against non-Muslims in many societies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Misguided religious preachers have spread insidious ideologies preaching segregation and a rejection of modern life and the secular state.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is surely the road to alienation, marginalisation and ruin.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In Singapore, we must stand united against such ideologues and ideologies, and against Islamophobia.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, we will continue our efforts to support our families and children, with an emphasis on early childhood education and helping the vulnerable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, we will enhance the socio-religious foundations of the community, by strengthening religious education and our key community institutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thirdly, we will build a future-ready community that embraces technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to ensure that every child has the best start in life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Good early childhood education is critical for a child's long-term development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We urge our parents to send their children to quality preschool education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question, the importance of early childhood education is why MENDAKI has, in recent years, focused more on supporting the development of children between zero and six years old.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Last year, MENDAKI held its inaugural Education Symposium, supported by the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) and the Learn SG seed fund.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over 250 participants benefited from discussions ranging from learning through play to preparing for primary school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Following the symposium, Mdm Irma Iryanti Juri, an adjunct lecturer at SEED Institute, which trains early childhood professionals, and Mdm Shaireen Selamat a doctoral researcher from the University of Warwick volunteered to lead the setting up of a network of professionals and educators from the preschool sector to share best practices and learn from one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, this network has become the MENDAKI Alliance of Preschool Professionals (MAPP), comprising about 30 professionals who actively support MENDAKI's School-Ready programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Playfest aims to generate awareness about the benefits of play and provide parents with ideas on setting up an age-appropriate stimulating learning environment at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to help more low-income families enroll their children into full-day childcare, as this provides a conducive environment for the child's development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The "Back-to-Work Women" programme is a key strategy in this effort, as it aims to help mothers to be gainfully employed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides enhancing the family's income, they will be able to tap on more childcare subsidies, and quality preschool education will, indeed, become more affordable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI will also work with ECDA and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) on ways to study how we can assist low-income families enroll their children in quality childcare and preschool education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Both Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about how we can best support our students' education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Twenty years ago, less than half of Malays entered post-secondary educational institutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are committed to help as many as we can to ensure that our young have a brighter future and can access more opportunities than before.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For primary and secondary school students, the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme (MTS), offers highly subsidised tuition sessions for students from lower-income families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To Assoc Prof Fatimah's question about students who face challenges in receiving help from Self-Help Groups, MENDAKI provides a wide range of assistance schemes, as long as they meet the criteria.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Any Muslim student can apply to MENDAKI for interest-free study loans and a wide range of bursaries and scholarships, while the best students, who excel in both academic and non-academic areas, would receive the Anugerah MENDAKI award.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are committed to helping all who deserve and seek assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As such, we are revising the income bands upwards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Muhammad Faisal Abdul Manap spoke about the Malay identity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For such matters, the Government takes a practical approach, bearing in mind the interest of the community and the wider society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: No matter how "Malayness" is defined, what matters is how we grow and sustain a strong community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And in this regard, the quality of our Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs), is, indeed, critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am glad that many of our MMOs, and even our mosques, are serving not only our community, but also reaching out to non-Malay/Muslims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MMOs like Jamiyah, 4PM and PPIS offer assistance to those in need, regardless of race or religion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Such efforts must continue and, as a community, we must support the good work of our MMOs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar and Mr Azmoon Ahmad asked about the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund (MMCDF), which was established to support all MMOs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In its last review in 2014, the Government re-allocated a portion of the matching grant for MENDAKI and the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP) towards increasing its matching grant for MMCDF, to provide greater support to MMOs that have less resources.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MMCDF also shifted its focus towards helping organisations build their capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Some of the initiatives that receive MMCDF funding include the Debt Advisory Centre by AMP, the Rising Star Project by PERTAPIS and the Family Therapy Institute by PPIS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While we support our established MMOs, I share Dr Intan Mokhtar's view that we must also provide the opportunities and support for our talented youths to step up and contribute to the greater good of both community and society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Community Leaders Forum (CLF) LABS allow youth-led organisations and groups to testbed innovative ideas with MENDAKI's seed funding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The inaugural Socialthon, held last July, brought together close to 100 youths to develop solutions in areas, such as startup culture, health and technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These platforms will help our youths hone their ideas and leadership skills, with the community and Singapore at heart.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Strong families are critical to the well-being of children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We amended AMLA last year to make it compulsory for minor couples to complete marriage preparation programmes and to obtain consent from parents or guardians, prior to making an application for marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To reply to Ms Rahayu Mahzam, MSF is working with the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) and INSPIRASI Hubs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Hubs are centres dedicated to preparing minor and young couples for marriage and to raise awareness of these new requirements and the importance of marriage preparation and parental support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MSF is also working with the Hubs to enhance the marriage preparation curriculum.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The programme will benefit about 200 minor couples every year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Vista Sakinah will collaborate with agencies serving low-income stepfamilies and waive the remarriage preparation programme fees for their participation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They will provide stepfamily awareness talks at key touchpoints, such as mosques and other community agencies, and leverage social media and radio.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Additionally, Vista Sakinah will enhance its programme effectiveness by strengthening its evidence-based content, building trainer capabilities, and enhancing its programme evaluation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our community is committed to developing strong institutions that support the socio-religious life of our community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I wish to assure Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Amrin Amin that we are committed to continually enhance our full-time madrasahs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our madrasahs play a dual role in nurturing future asatizahs for the community, and in preparing those who opt for careers in the non-religious sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will share plans to strengthen two of our madrasahs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Madrasah Wak Tanjong, founded by the late Ustaz Mohd Noor bin Taib, is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Its students have a history of excelling in religious studies and taking up religious leadership roles in the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One example is Ustazah Hilwani binte Mohammad Abdul Halim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She is the daughter of the late Ustaz Mohammad Abdul Halim, who was the Principal of Madrasah Wak Tanjong for five years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She does her late father proud by teaching Islamic Jurisprudence and Arabic at Madrasah Wak Tanjong.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hilwani holds a Bachelor's Degree in Islamic Jurisprudence from the University of Jordan, but she is determined to better herself as a teacher.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She is now enrolled in a specialist diploma programme in Applied Learning and Teaching at Republic Polytechnic under MUIS' sponsorship and will graduate in August this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We wish Hilwani all the best and look forward to her wider contributions to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This strong support signals MUIS' ongoing commitment to further professionalise and strengthen the madrasah sector as a whole.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am also happy to present the design of the new Madrasah Al Arabiah Al Islamiah campus.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It has a sustainable and green design that is complemented with Islamic and nusantara architecture.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I urge the community to support the madrasah's fundraising efforts to ensure that the campus can be operational by 2020.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Similarly, over 500 students received the Madrasah Student Awards just last month in recognition of their educational excellence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: School leaders, IB coordinators and teachers have been hard at work in equipping themselves with the necessary skills and qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Third, MUIS has worked with the madrasahs to strengthen the holistic development of their students, so that they are exposed to areas, such as youth volunteerism, service learning projects and outdoor education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want our students to go beyond the classroom, to interact with and contribute to the larger Singapore society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, our madrasah graduates are our future asatizahs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In this regard, we have been looking into plans to develop an Islamic college in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked for an update.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, for example, both Al-Azhar University and the University of Jordan traditionally produce religious teachers, while the latter also trains its students with broad-based skills for employability in the non-religious sector for the wider economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Turkish universities take an academic approach in teaching classical Islamic sciences and the humanities, while its Diyanet, or the Turkish central religious authority, separately provides religious vocational training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the other hand, Zaytuna College and Notre Dame University in the US, and McGill University in Canada, take a rigorous, academic approach to produce scholars.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The different learning approaches provide useful learning points and each is suited to its own society and context.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: An Islamic college in Singapore would adapt appropriate features from overseas institutions, so that we will, in time, produce Islamic teachers and scholars who balance a deep learning of Islamic sciences with broad-based skills and knowledge and, more importantly, are rooted in the belief and practice of Islam in Singapore's multi-religious and multiracial context.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also took the opportunity to meet our Singaporean students studying in these institutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The students highlighted how social issues have become more complex and perspectives are more diverse.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They emphasised how, for Singapore, religious teachers must be able to guide Muslims in living out the religion as members of our modern, plural society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They shared their concerns about employability, safety and the cost of education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I appreciate their frank views, which we will consider carefully in developing a high-quality tertiary education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But with hard work and taking the time to carefully study this undertaking, I am confident that we can develop an institution that will nurture future asatizahs whom our community looks up to and supports wholeheartedly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the coming months, MUIS will be engaging the community for their views so that our first Islamic college in Singapore will be a centre of excellence for the learning of Islam that we can all be proud of.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While we plan for the future of religious education, we wish to encourage talented young asatizahs to engage our youths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I agree with Mr Zainal Sapari that we must inoculate our young against extremist and segregationist views.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must not allow such ideologies to take root in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must start early and focus on upstream work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ustaz Tarmizi Wahid belongs to this pioneer batch.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He is the CEO and founder of Safinah Institute, a private Islamic learning centre with a strong digital media presence, especially on Instagram.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Safinah also operates a digital device-friendly platform called Soul Academy, where participants can virtually interact and discuss issues with trainers and peers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: AYN has been active in increasing outreach both online and offline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In October 2017, they collaborated with the Religious Rehabilitation Group (RRG), and the Singapore Islamic Scholars and Religious Teachers Association (PERGAS) to organise a Seminar on Strengthening the Religious Resilience of the Singapore Muslim Community for about 300 asatizahs and community leaders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In December, they produced a video series #TheProphetIKnow, featuring the AYN asatizahs promoting the values that the Prophet stood for and how Muslims contribute to the larger society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This video production was done following AYN's participation in a workshop on effective counter-narrative and digital engagements conducted by Google Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS has grown its scope of work in serving the socio-religious needs of the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes increasing prayer spaces in mosques, distributing zakat and facilitating haj and korban.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In doing so, MUIS has endeavoured to maintain strong partnerships with key community stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The events of September 11, the spectre of extremism and the emergence of charismatic Internet-age radical ideologues have made MUIS’ mission all the more difficult.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But MUIS has stayed the course in nurturing a Singapore Muslim Identity, one that honours the Islamic faith, the aspirations of our community, and the relationships and identities that bind us to Singapore, our home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim asked about plans for this significant milestone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The theme "Semarak Langkah, Berjiwa Rahmah" or "Striving with Confidence, Serving with Compassion" is apt in portraying the spirit of MUIS' service to the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS is currently engaging the community through the ongoing MUIS50 conversations for ideas to strengthen MUIS for the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More details will be shared at MUIS' Work Plan Seminar next month.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to elaborate on our third strategy of forging a future-ready community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about what more we can do to support our students and workers better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI partnered the three ITE colleges for its Future First Programme (FFP).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI will be expanding the programme to even more ITE students, partnering polytechnics and the wider youth community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This would include the launch of a Future-Ready Starter Kit in August 2018 on workplace expectations, and strategies to remain relevant in the future economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: With improving educational attainment by Malay students, we have seen a higher proportion of PMETs in the Malay workforce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Of these, about two-thirds are associate professionals and technicians.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also see that Malays have a higher than proportional share of placements under the Adapt and Grow initiative, which includes the career centres run by Workforce Singapore and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) e2i.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Committee has leveraged key platforms, such as SENSE PMET Jobfair@Grassroots Club and "Secangkir Kopi bersama MENDAKI" dialogue and networking session.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Committee produced and distributed more than 3,000 copies of the "Handy Guidebook for PMETs" to raise awareness on support schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Committee intends to do more engagements, with four "JUMP!

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Career Fairs” to offer assistance and raise awareness about growth sectors in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MUIS and MENDAKI have already started using digital tools to improve service delivery and accessibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, MUIS has placed the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) procedures online, on the LicenceOne portal, to make it easier for registration and to undertake data analytics on the asatizah sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI's Tuition Scheme Online Programme Registration System and Loan Management System have enhanced user convenience and organisation productivity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The data collected through tuition registration enables the team to analyse the profiles of students and their families and helps us to tailor programmes and outreach according to students' performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am pleased to share that MENDAKI has set up a Digital Transformation Department that will help facilitate the digital transformation of our MMOs so that the community can ultimately benefit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One MMO that has started its digitalisation journey is PPIS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: PPIS currently serves about 500 students across seven centres and they want to attract more families with preschool-going children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: PPIS is partnering MENDAKI on a data-analytics project to better understand the profiles and needs of client families, so that PPIS can offer higher quality and relevant services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Going digital is vital for our SMEs, too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I had the opportunity to engage members of the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is heartening to see Malay/Muslim SMEs, such as Frozi, a food and beverage (F&B) establishment that serves frozen yogurt, and Spear Security Force, a security company making good progress with their first use of digital solutions to increase revenue and improve productivity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to encourage more, if not all, Malay/Muslim SMEs to take that critical first step.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have been working with SME Centre@SMCCI, supported by the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) SME Digital Tech Hub, to organise workshops for members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: With SMCCI taking the lead to help their members tap on SMEs Go Digital programme, I believe more Malay/Muslim SMEs will come on board.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We can also use digital technology to harness the richness of our heritage and culture.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Kampong Glam has historically been an open community and welcomes people of different ages and cultures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to see if we can enhance the customer and retail experience and transform the overall visitor experience at Kampong Glam.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For a start, we will guide Kampong Glam merchants on how they can digitalise themselves to improve their business operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, there are already existing merchants doing so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Wardah sells a wide range of books from Islamic history to philosophy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It actively uses social media, and it has also digitalised its processes so that data accounting is integrated between its physical and online stores.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The presence of an online store not only directs traffic to the physical store but boosts its reach to overseas customers in Malaysia and Brunei.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Digitalisation will be a key anchor for our community's future growth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is why I urge our workforce to be future-ready, and our community organisations and SMEs to transform, so that we and our future generations can continue to achieve our hopes and aspirations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, the Malay/Muslim community continues to move forward with much confidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In line with efforts to progress with the other communities, I have drafted three key strategies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, supporting the institution of family, with a special emphasis on early childhood education, apart from helping vulnerable families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, enhancing the socio-religious foundations of the community by strengthening religious education and our religious institutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Third, building a Malay/Muslim community which embraces technology so that they are ready for new types of jobs and various opportunities that are available in the Digital Economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Strong families form a pillar of the nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We want to ensure that every child in Singapore is given the best possible start in life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Therefore, good quality preschools are critical for a child's long-term development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, MENDAKI is now focused on the development of young children from zero to six years old to help Malay/Muslim parents prepare their children for primary school in reading, writing and arithmetic, as well as being socially and emotionally ready.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MENDAKI will work with experts in this sector to increase public awareness and share best practices amongst educators and professionals as well as parents on the importance of early childhood education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, learning through play and inculcating a maker's mindset are not new concepts to the Malay community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our traditional pantuns and heritage songs display the wisdom of our forefathers in moulding children from a tender age.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, the song "Satu satu Aku Sayang Ibu" (Number One – I Love Mummy) and "Satu Tangan Bilangan Lima" (One Hand Shows Five) introduces number concepts and counting through songs, besides teaching the importance of family.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The song "Layang-Layang" (Kites) promotes a culture of tinkering through the precise skill of kite making.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, we hope events like "PlayFest" for preschool children can complement our efforts to provide quality education that is engaging for our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This revision means that more Malay students from low-income families are eligible for subsidies while pursuing diplomas or university degrees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will take effect from this academic year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The package includes extension to the lease at its current premises at Sims Avenue for the next 30 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In addition, extra funding will be provided to strengthen its curriculum and for the professional development of staff.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am also happy to present the beautiful design of Madrasah Al-Arabiah Al-Islamiah's new campus, which is expected to be ready by 2020.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I look forward to the community's full support in the upcoming fundraising efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, one of the main objectives of our madrasahs is to produce religious teachers who can guide the local Muslim community in navigating a fast-paced and challenging world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Together with the staff of MUIS, I visited several well-known universities in the Middle East like Egypt, Jordan and Turkey, as well as in America and Canada.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We gained many learning points from these visits.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: What stood out the most are the unique pedagogical approach and curricula that are suited to the context of each country and society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will assess all these learning points and the salient ones will be incorporated into our plans for the Islamic college, so that we can produce religious teachers who are confident, knowledgeable in Islamic studies and other skills, such as counselling or social work, conscious about the reality of challenges in the contemporary world and, more importantly, appreciate the context of living in Singapore's plural society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This culture must also be swiftly embraced by our businesses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: If they do not transform their businesses quickly through technology, I am concerned that many Malay businesses passed down through the generations, including our delicious nasi padang, will disappear in the face of stiff competition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For many years, this area is popular among tourists and locals alike.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Sultan Mosque, the Istana Kampong Gelam, the Gedung Kuning, and the surrounding areas which once formed the transit area for Haj pilgrims in yesteryears, have their own hidden attractions and stories to share.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Every visitor can enjoy a unique immersive experience, including the chance to take a journey through our rich heritage, which has been our shared pride and joy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Chairman, the intent behind these efforts is not simply about taking advantage of technology merely on a surface level; rather, it reflects a deeper genuine commitment of the Malay/Muslim community to continue strengthening ourselves, our families and our community in line with our nation's development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Let us move forward as described in the following pantun: We went to the fields; the harvest done at last, The time to roll up our sleeves has passed; We came to this Chamber; deliberations are over, It is time to overcome our challenges, together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: (In English): Sir, in closing, the Malay community has come a long way on its journey towards a Community of Excellence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Over the years, we have painstakingly laid the building blocks for current and future generations to grow and realise their fullest potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But, Sir, the journey has not always been smooth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It was with hard work and sacrifice that we achieved progress against the odds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It was with pride and love that we stayed strong as a community honouring our traditions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It was with wisdom and courage that we forged our own model of what it means to be Muslim in modern, multiracial and multi-religious Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The statistics show that we have come very far.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But one does not see hopes and dreams nor struggles and victories in statistics alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For me, what gives me relentless optimism in our future is in the life stories of so many Malay/Muslim families that I have met who have overcome immense odds and made out better lives through their efforts in the everyday.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, I return to the story of Mr Fadli Sidek, whom I spoke about in my MCI COS speech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: His is a story of gumption and resilience, of not wanting to accept defeat, and of achieving his dream in an emerging growth area.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: He is in cybersecurity, a field that is growing and is a key enabler in our vision to be a Smart Nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fadli, and many like him, embody all that we believe in and the values and principles that have gotten us here thus far.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We cannot truly say that we have arrived until we have paved the way for all those around us to succeed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is our collective responsibility to ensure that no one gets left behind.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I call upon those who have achieved a measure of success to step forward and inspire others around you.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have been blessed with selfless and dedicated community and religious leaders who have worked tirelessly in their own capacities, be it in our mosques, madrasahs, community and voluntary organisations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We need more to come forward to contribute in whatever way you can.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As the Prime Minister had mentioned in his New Year message, let us use the occasion of the Bicentennial Celebrations next year to reflect on what it means to be a Singaporean.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As we move forward as a community in a multiracial nation within the larger Nusantara, let us ponder on the values that we hold dear as a community, on all the subtle things that define who we are, and on all those links that we have built, as well as the many that we have yet to build, with those around us and in the region.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am proud and honoured to have been a part of this journey, working hand in hand with all of you.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Much remains to be done, and we all need to continue to play our part, in whatever way we can.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Let us work together, as one people, always striving to make Singapore the best home for us all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, the CDCs that were started 20 years ago to assist the needy, bond the people and connect the community are more relevant today than ever before.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With an ageing population and the onset of disruptions brought about by technology, there is a greater need for assistance, stability and training to help Singaporeans stay relevant with the new skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The personalised My SkillsFuture Portal was launched and the five CDCs brought SkillsFuture advice and career roadshows into the heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These initiatives provide Singaporeans with online and offline assistance as well as up-to-date information on training and job opportunities and a platform to chart their learning and career paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These efforts support the work of the Future Economy Council by empowering and equipping Singaporeans with opportunities to learn, adapt and upskill as our economy restructures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This one-stop centre offers support in areas like business diagnosis, networking and capability-building workshops.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The CDCs will expand our outreach to improve our people's skills, resilience and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretaries to the Ministers for Education and Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is our mission to develop and strengthen our communities to keep our nation united and cohesive.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, PA is a Statutory Board that supports the elected Government of the day in implementing its policies and programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Its mission is to promote social cohesion and racial harmony and connect the people and the Government.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Through its community-bonding programmes, PA also explains and gathers citizens’ concerns and feedback on Government policies so that we can be a responsive and responsible Government.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do not presume that Opposition MPs believe that they will be willing or able to execute this role for the Government of the day.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To address Mr Pritam Singh's question, MPs have their roles to play, such as representing their constituents' views in Parliament and running the Town Council where the MPs have substantial responsibility in the administration and maintenance of public housing estates.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Government agencies will work with the respective MPs and grassroots advisers on matters related to their respective roles.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On Mr Faisal Manap's points, let me make the following points.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, anyone can write to the Government agencies and anyone can help anyone else to write to the Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And I believe that Government agencies have also received letters from Mr Leon Perera and other people who have previously stood in elections.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I am confident that the agencies will know who is the elected MP for that constituency and give the matter due consideration.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yes, indeed, we do appoint people with diverse experiences and background to the Citizens Consultative Committees (CCCs).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The key criteria are that we believe that the person can help contribute to the mission of PA, which is to bond our people and help the Government of the day which governs the country, to make us a much more responsive Government.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Government agencies will work with community organisations to meet the needs and to serve the needs of the community where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Just one clarification with the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: First of all, I thank the Minister for the good news about the change or revision of income eligibility criteria.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We do not have the exact figure at this point in time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Once the applications open, then we will see the numbers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We expect that we will be able to deal with all those cases.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Chairman, the question is directed to Minister Chan Chun Sing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I did not hear or I may have missed it out, but I do not think I am quite clear on the relationship between the CDC and the Town Council, and the Opposition Town Council, in particular.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is it different from, let us say, the PA grassroots adviser and the Town Council?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Maybe I will try to use a more specific example.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: For example, during a community festival, say, Hari Raya or Chinese New Year, you see banners that are put on lamp posts and there is a CDC logo at the bottom of the lamp post; and sometimes, in other towns, you will see the Town Council logo there as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm whether there is co-funding involved in the putting up of those banners and can an Opposition Town Council tap on the co-funding from the CDCs?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, to make the position very clear, Government agencies do not, I say Government agencies do not, fund political outreach for any political party.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Government agencies will work with various community partners to serve the needs of the community.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But the issue is that the Town Council is not a political entity.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not using the logo of the political party to celebrate this festival, for example.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is essentially the CDC logo and the Town Council logo.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Aljunied Town Council reaches out to all residents, regardless of their political affiliation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, if the activity is organised by the CC, if that is what the Member is asking for, then they put their logo there; if the Town Council organises your activity, you put your logo there.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do apologise if I have not been clear for some reason.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is not an activity that is being organised.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It is a banner that is put up to celebrate a festival.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It could be Deepavali, it could be Chinese New Year, saying "Best wishes to all residents from the CDC and from the Town Council".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I am just enquiring whether it can be done in the case of an Opposition Town Council.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because there is no political involvement, there is no political activity at all.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Then, I suggest maybe you work with the respective CDC.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The issue is: would there be an objection from the Government, would there be an objection from the Mayors to have this sort of collaboration with an Opposition Town Council?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because if the Minister says that it should not be a problem, I am pretty sure the Mayors would not object, as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us separate the Government duties from anything that connotes political outreach.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Government of the day must be very careful that whenever it spends its money, whenever it does its outreach, it does not overstep its bound to the political realm.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, if there is any collaboration between the Town Council with any of the Government agencies, I think it is best to take up the case specifically.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, I believe, in the history of Aljunied Town Council, you have worked with various Government agencies to do various things to serve the community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This includes, for example, during the dengue outbreak, I believe Aljunied Town Council worked with the National Environment Agency (NEA) for the functions that it was supposed to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: During the GST hike, I do not presume that the Aljunied Town Council will work with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to do outreach on explaining that, because it will put the Member in a very difficult position.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where it is appropriate, the agencies will work to serve the community of the day.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: One is for Minister Yaacob Ibrahim and one for Minister Chan Chun Sing.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: For Minister Chan Chun Sing, my speech was to ask for clarification.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: It was not about asking or clarifying about whether any Government agencies accept letters written by any political party members.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The Minister mentioned Mr Leon Perera, who is also a Non-Constituency MP (NCMP).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: My question is about the issue of politicisation and conflict of interest where a particular grassroots adviser goes for house visits, invites the people to come to his MPS which is being held in a political party branch office and the letter written on behalf of the residents is signed off by this particular person who holds two designations: grassroots adviser and political party branch chairman, and the letterhead being used for this appeal letter bears the name of the political party.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I just want to know, from the Minister's point of view, is there any element of politicisation as well as conflict of interest in this particular example that I have mentioned?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, hopefully, the Minister can give a direct answer to this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But certainly, what we want to do is to continue to honour the memory of the founder of the madrasah and the identity of the madrasah.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would leave it to MUIS and both madrasahs to work out the details.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I think we should be happy that we have come to this conclusion that we are now able to move MWTI forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They will retain their name, they will retain their identity and, if they want to tap on some of the best things that we have done in the Joint Madrasah System (JMS), I will leave it to the board to do so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But in the event that the person says, "Oh, I want to go to the PAP branch", then the protocol for them is very simple.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The PAP branch chairman can help you draft the letter, you can sign off the letter, we can help you send the thing, but even if the PAP branch provides the cover letter, he is not the elected MP for that constituency.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I am sure that agencies would know who the elected MP is in that constituency.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, many of us have multiple capacities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We sometimes write letters to our own Ministries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But there is a clear difference when you write letters as an MP, as you are performing your MP duty, your political role.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If you are the Minister in charge of that Ministry, you have to consider and let your staff consider the merits of the case based on that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, many of us will have multiple hats.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But all of us, all of us, must be very clear as to how we separate those responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I would just like to ask the Minister: this particular grassroots adviser goes for house visits, invites residents to come to see him at his MPS which is being held in a political party branch, as well as the letters sent out being signed by him with his designation as a political party branch chairman.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I would just like to know whether there is any element of politicisation and conflict of interest in the role of the grassroots adviser in this particular case.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me repeat myself: that grassroots adviser, the first thing is to advise his residents to go and see his MP for any representation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If the resident says that, on top of that, he does not want to go and see his MP, he is at liberty to go to the branch.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But when he goes to the branch, he must understand that the branch chairman who writes the letter for him or helps him draft the letter and he signed it himself or gave him a cover letter, that is not a MP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Then when the agencies receive the letters, they will know that, in this particular case, who is the MP who is representing the resident and who is the NCMP or not elected MP who is helping them to draft the letter.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The agencies will give the appropriate due consideration for the matter at hand.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
