speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the lab, Joseph went through a free onboarding session comprising a series of non-invasive assessments on body composition and other health markers, for an overview of his current health status.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At almost 126 kilogrammes (kg) then, our Active Health experts worked with Joseph to set his personal health and wellness goals and advised him to start making small changes to his lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Joseph, who used to have a largely sedentary lifestyle, started walking more, watching his diet and sleeping better.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A newspaper reported his case in February and mentioned that he has lost three kg in one month.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: His exercise comprises running interval trainings, strength workouts and stretching exercises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Like Joseph, you may be looking to manage your weight better; you may be a senior looking to enhance your flexibility; you may be a working adult looking for ways to keep a balanced and healthy lifestyle amid a busy schedule.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Active Health is for you, is for everyone, regardless of who you are and what your health and wellness goals are.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To kickstart your personal Active Health journey, all you have to do is visit an Active Health Lab.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We also plan to introduce two Mobile Labs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Working with PA, we will bring these Mobile Labs to the CC and Residents' Committee (RC) spaces as well as Sports-in-Precinct facilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Once onboarded with your baseline health indicators assessed, you can choose from a wide range of sports and physical activity programmes offered by ActiveSG at our sports centres across Singapore to pursue your health goals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You can also arrange for follow-up sessions with our Active Health experts to check on your progress and obtain feedback that can help you and your doctor plan for medical follow-ups, if necessary.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are also developing a mobile platform through which you, your doctor and the Active Health expert will be able to track and monitor your health progress beyond the clinic and the lab.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You can also connect with your family, friends and other Active Health users for mutual support, as well as sign up for ActiveSG programmes or book sports facilities to stay active together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With Active Health, we want to create a holistic support system where Singaporeans proactively take ownership of their health, engage in physical activity and be the social reinforcement that we all need to stay healthy and active.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We can be a nation of healthy, active and engaged citizens, where we help one another live better.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ultimately, shared identity and shared experiences must translate into action if they are to add up to a strong society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we see what we have in common, when we embrace those different from ourselves, we should also grow to care and feel responsible for one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the face of a more complex and unpredictable future, we need every Singaporean to step up and be a part of the answer that the society needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singaporeans are willing, whether it is to help the vulnerable or disadvantaged, or give to social causes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But there is a gap between desire and action.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many youths have also deemed helping the less fortunate and contributing to society as very important life goals, but fewer thought that active involvement in volunteer work was important.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Yesterday, Minister Desmond Lee, Minister Gan Kim Yong and I spoke about building a more caring and inclusive home for every Singaporean through SG Cares.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As Minister Heng Swee Keat highlighted in his Budget Statement, the SG Cares movement is about bringing diverse people together to achieve a greater collective impact.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In line with SG Cares, we will continue to expand volunteering opportunities provided through sports, heritage and arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To cultivate a caring society, we will also ensure that we have a strong charity sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will elaborate on these efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chairman, please allow me to conclude in Mandarin.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Together, we can construct a more effective social safety net and nurture a more caring and supportive society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If we can be more considerate and extend a helping hand to others when we are able to, then we will be building a more resilient Singapore, a country where our elders will be taken care of, the able-bodied can contribute meaningfully, our young can grow and develop, and our vulnerable members will be supported.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I will display some slides.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Minister Grace Fu highlighted that a key focus area for MCCY this year is to partner Singaporeans in building a home where we care for and look out for others.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As the Minister shared, our volunteerism and philanthropy rates have grown.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: More Singaporeans are prepared to put into action their desire to do good for others.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In line with the broader SG Cares objective of creating a caring and inclusive home for all, I will share how MCCY is partnering Singaporeans to build a strong civic culture of care, consideration and contribution across the various domains under our Ministry.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked how the arts and heritage can be used to encourage inclusiveness.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Through our ArtReach initiative, we will continue to promote arts access to underserved communities for wellness and to build social connections.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For example, the National Arts Council (NAC) has partnered the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to promote the well-being and active ageing of seniors by integrating arts into community care.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Following our visual arts residency pilot in nine nursing homes last year, NAC and AIC will develop more arts-based resources to continue building capabilities in this sector.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Befrienders Arts Toolkit will be launched in June to provide social service organisations with arts-based activity ideas to support the process of befriending seniors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is to support collaborations between social service organisations and the arts community, to benefit isolated seniors, persons with disabilities and vulnerable youths.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Earlier this year, I was pleased to attend the launch of "Is Anyone Home?", an exhibition by Superhero Me, a ground-up inclusive arts movement.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The exhibition featured the imaginative artworks and stories of children from diverse backgrounds, including children with special needs and those from low-income families.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I was moved to see how these budding artists interpreted childhood and expressed their hopes and dreams.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Projects like these use arts as a powerful means to engage children, build their confidence and realise their potential.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Social service organisations can tap on the WeCare Arts Fund to work with artists to develop interactive arts workshops customised to the needs and interests of their beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One example is Jia Ying Senior Activity Centre, which participated in a programme where seniors paired up with youths on art-making.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The seniors, who were previously isolated, are now making new friends and have developed a more positive mindset and outlook on life.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also continue to improve arts access and opportunities for Persons with Disabilities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This month, we will host the first Arts and Disability International Conference, co-organised by NAC and Very Special Arts (VSA) Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will facilitate the sharing of best practices and innovative approaches to promote inclusivity in the arts.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Conference is part of the inaugural True Colours Festival, which will showcase artists with disabilities from Singapore and the Asia Pacific.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Our shared heritage is what binds us as a nation, and it belongs to us all.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Minister spoke about increasing accessibility to our museums and heritage institutions as part of Our SG Heritage Plan.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The first step is to audit the accessibility of our museums to identify universal design solutions and assistive technologies for different groups.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To actively engage audiences at our heritage spaces, our HeritageCares programmes provide beneficiaries of social service organisations with opportunities that encourage meaningful intergenerational bonding, enhance social skills, provide quality educational experiences and promote active ageing.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Workshops and programmes, such as guided trails of historical sites, are tailored to meet the needs of families in-need, adults and children with special needs, vulnerable youths and seniors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One new initiative under Our SG Heritage Plan is for our heritage institutions to be "Silver Hubs", to promote active ageing and intergenerational interactions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will offer opportunities for seniors to be active participants in our heritage by volunteering as guides and facilitators in galleries.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A Conversation Starter Kit was also piloted last year for seniors to share their personal and community experiences amongst Singaporeans across all ages.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Our youths play a critical role in growing a strong civic culture of care, consideration and contribution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Youth Corps Singapore (YCS) was established to develop youth volunteers and leaders and inspire more youths to give back to the community through causes, such as social service, education, environment, arts, sports and heritage.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: YCS also offers opportunities to volunteer overseas through the Youth Expedition Project (YEP).

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One example is Team Nias, a group of 16 youths from Nanyang Technological University (NTU) who embarked on a mission to install solar panels in Nias, Indonesia.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Here, we see some of them in action, teaching English to the local kids.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Unfortunately, the solar panels did not arrive in time.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Undeterred, the team used their own pocket money to return the following week to install the panels.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In this programme, youth leaders will be deployed to social service organisations serving communities with special needs, the young and vulnerable, and the elderly.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The youths will be equipped with skills in community engagement, eldercare and volunteer management, so that they can help spread the culture of volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We recognise that not all youths have the resources or opportunity to participate in these development programmes while in school.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Hence, we will explore ways to make programmes, such as YEP and the Outward Bound School, more financially accessible and open up opportunities for more youths outside school to apply.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In the realm of sports, we are encouraging Singaporeans to give back through Team Nila.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Team Nila volunteers are our capacity and community multipliers who mobilise a wider group of residents on the ground.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am pleased to see strong representation of volunteers across races and age groups, from youths to seniors, passionate about bringing the benefit of sport to their neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Darryl David asked about our plans to develop Team Nila.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Since 2014, SportSG has been transforming Team Nila volunteers into community and events leaders.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have volunteers actively supporting the physical and mental development of children and youths in their roles as assistant coaches with ActiveSG Academies and Clubs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This number is set to grow as more academies and clubs are introduced.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There are plans for Team Nila volunteers to assist allied health trained experts in helping residents take ownership of their health and wellness.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SportSG will continue to equip Team Nila with the necessary skills through structured training plans.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For example, this year we will see about 500 volunteers undergo various WSQ training programmes in service excellence, leadership and people management.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how sports help improve the lives of seniors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Being a part of Team Nila has enabled our seniors to maintain friendships and social circles of like-minded individuals and allowed them to derive satisfaction from sports volunteerism.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One example is the sprightly Mdm Hajjah Zubaidah Binte Abdul Ghani, a 64-year-old senior assistant at Tan Tock Seng Hospital who finds it meaningful to be a Team Nila volunteer.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To recognise outstanding volunteers who have embodied the spirit of giving and contributed actively, SportSG has launched two new awards on 1 January, namely, the Outstanding Team Nila and Team Nila Tiered Awards.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We hope to see more Singaporeans step up to volunteer, whether as part of Team Nila, or for a cause close to their hearts.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Ms Joan Pereira also asked how sports can be used to improve the lives of those in need, such as at-risk youths, and how MCCY is working with the Public-People-Private sectors to broaden outreach and engagement.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Since the launch of SportCares in 2012, schools, community groups, corporates and individuals have come together to support sports initiatives that benefit and transform vulnerable communities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We provide platforms that facilitate joint stewardship and active citizenry.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One good example is Hands to Hearts, a community crafting project which also exemplifies 3P collaboration.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In 2017, Hands to Hearts saw SportCares youths take the lead to sew tactile activity pillows for seniors with Alzheimer's.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They were joined by 2,000 volunteers, including staff from corporate bodies, such as the United Overseas Bank (UOB) and ComfortDelGro, as well as students from Tanglin Trust International School and Madrasah Aljunied.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The project showed us that that we can achieve more if we work together.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will continue to partner our stakeholders to reach out to the underserved.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will extend this sense of shared endeavour amongst our partners via the development and adoption of the new HEARTS framework.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This framework was developed with our partner organisations and is intended to help youths chart a positive course in their lives.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To be launched in April, the pilot framework will be shared with social service organisations and schools in the form of a handy toolkit.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The idea is to provide community practitioners with easy-to-use resources to design sport-based social development programmes for youths.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Complementing this will be eight SportCares Partner Schemes that will provide support and resources to community groups, IHLs, NSAs and corporates to "do good" through sport.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To further promote inclusivity, the Disability Sports Master Plan aims to expand access and opportunities for sports participation to all, regardless of abilities, and build public awareness of disability sports.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have annual platforms, like the Inclusive Sports Festival, that help create greater awareness for disability sports, such as wheelchair rugby.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SportSG will continue to strengthen its partnership with disability sports organisations, such as the Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC) and Special Olympics Singapore, as well as with Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To date, SportSG has connected mainstream schools, such as Bowen Secondary, to social service organisations, such as MINDSville Napiri Training Centre, through adaptive sports.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SportSG is also working with Special Education (SPED) schools, such as Lighthouse School, to introduce sports as co-curricular activity options.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Through Our Singapore Fund, we will continue to encourage our people to come together to make Singapore a better home.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Fund aims to nurture our Singapore identity and values, and support ground-up initiatives by citizens.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have also simplified our processes to make it easier for more people to apply for the fund.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Beyond numbers, each project demonstrates how Singaporeans are taking the initiative to reach out, across age, income or race, to care for one another as one people.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: An example is Project Caring with Authenticity and Respect for Elders (CARE) which rallies volunteers to visit and befriend isolated seniors.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: During the lunar new year, Project CARE teamed up with Carousell, an online marketplace platform, to mobilise the community to donate items to the elderly in need.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To cultivate a caring society, we require a strong charity sector that inspires confidence and encourages people to step forward and contribute with peace of mind.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Darryl David asked about our plans on helping smaller charities better comply with regulations and our plans to regulate and manage online donations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will work to ensure a safe and transparent giving environment through cooperation and partnership with the various charitable bodies in two main areas.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: One, we will strengthen smaller charities’ regulatory compliance through co-regulation and more targeted guidance.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: With the launch of the refined Code of Governance in 2017, we will continue our efforts to organise sharing sessions on the Code for specific sectors, such as the Malay/Muslim organisations and Hindu charities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Last year, we held sessions for churches, Chinese temples and arts and heritage charities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Two, we will be enhancing safer giving measures, and heightening transparency and accountability through three means.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To enhance the disclosure practices of charities and facilitate donors in their giving decisions, the Commissioner of Charities will develop a visibility guide to be launched in mid-2018.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will help charities put out key information, such as use of donations and activities of a charity, in a simple manner.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Second, a safer giving campaign will be launched in phases from June 2018.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This follows the findings of an informed giving survey conducted last year.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The campaign is in addition to ongoing initiatives to promote safer giving and provide advisories on what to look out for and questions to ask in relation to online appeals.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also ramp up our education efforts on safer giving, with targeted outreach to the elderly and working adults.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Third, we have the Code of Practice for Crowdfunding Platforms, which we have co-developed with key crowdfunding platforms to ensure a safer online giving environment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Launched in January this year by the Minister, the Code of Practice will be implemented over the course of the year.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Minister Heng Swee Keat has pointed out that a good society is one with a spirit of caring, where we all feel responsibility towards one another.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Looking ahead, MCCY will continue to work closely with our partners and fellow Singaporeans to make Singapore a caring and inclusive home.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I will display some slides.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Minister and Senior Minister of State highlighted the role of MCCY in bringing our nation together and partnering our citizens to make Singapore a better home, and a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Looking forward, we aim to build a buoyant Singapore, a nation that is confident in our future.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through our work in the arts and sports sectors, and our continued investment in our youths, our people can be confident that this is a place we can lead fulfilling lives and pursue our dreams.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun suggested that we review our achievements under the Arts and Culture Strategic Review (ACSR).

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Launched in 2010, the ACSR builds on the foundations laid by the Advisory Council on Culture and the Arts and the Renaissance City Plans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Its 2025 vision is for Singapore to be a nation of cultured and gracious people, at home with our heritage, proud of our Singaporean identity by (a) bringing arts and culture to everyone, everywhere, every day; and (b) building capabilities to achieve excellence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Since the ACSR recommendations were released in 2012, we have introduced a range of initiatives to increase accessibility to arts and culture and invested in excellence.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The arts scene is more vibrant today, with more Singaporeans recognising the value of the arts to the individual, community and our larger Singapore society, and more agreeing that the arts help to improve our lives.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We have already started engaging the arts community, including Mr Kok Heng Leun, on the broad direction of these plans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to grow opportunities in audience development, community arts, arts education, capability development, internationalisation, as well as research and documentation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the meantime, we have already started to work on a few areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our efforts in the literary arts scene have resulted in a strong talent base, especially in English, and more platforms for our writers to reach their readers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: However, there remains much room for us to promote the Chinese, Malay and Tamil literary arts.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These literary works are written in our four official languages.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our primary and secondary school students will be able to read local literary works from local writers like Francis Wong, Huang Shu Jun and Ai Yu.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that the early exposure to SingLit will allow them to develop a sustained interest in local literary works.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These local stories will also serve as a shared experience as they grow up.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will be using digital technology to grow support for local arts, including Singapore music.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This digital platform will allow the public to listen to Singapore music from different genres, languages and decades.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Hear65 will, therefore, be a platform that appeals to both the young and old.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: There will be local classics from my parents’ generation, like songs by Huang Qing Yuan and Poon Sow Keng.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Also, there will be familiar songs from Liang Wern Fook and Kit Chan for Singaporeans around my age.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Younger audiences will be able to listen to famous pop songs from Tanya Chua, Stephanie Sun and JJ Lin.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With access to musical works from more than 350 local musicians, we hope more Singaporeans will follow our local music and continue to develop our Singapore music scene.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In English): Music is an integral part of Singaporeans’ lives.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Hear65, a national music movement that will be launched next month in collaboration with local music media company Bandwagon, will profile homegrown music talents to Singapore and international audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Users can look forward to an online, interactive platform that showcases music performed by local artists, such as The Quests, Anita Sarawak, Taufik Batisah, Vanessa Fernandez, Shabir Alam and Gentle Bones.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Hear65 will offer access to music on streaming platforms and crowdsourced reviews of the featured content.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Hear65 will also partner private and public stakeholders, such as the Esplanade, to create more buzz around Singapore music.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the area of Visual Art, we would like the public to enjoy our artists’ work as part of daily life.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Using artworks to enliven our urban landscape is one approach, as Dr Lim Wee Kiak has pointed out.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For SG50, we commissioned three public artworks in the Civic District under the Public Art Trust.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In commemoration of Singapore’s Bicentennial next year, two new signature public artworks will also be commissioned in community spaces.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to commission one signature public artwork per year thereafter under the Trust.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond this, we have freed up more sites for artists to create public art in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To date, more than 30 sites have been secured, including spaces in town centres and sports centres in Ang Mo Kio, Bedok, Bukit Panjang, Clementi and Woodlands.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This initial list of sites will be released in the middle of this year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I encourage interested venue owners to get in touch with NAC if you have suitable spaces that can be included.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Likewise, we encourage artists to consider these sites and submit proposals through the Public Art Trust website.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also launch public art trails and guided tours beyond the Civic District and Central Business District.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, we will have more public art programmes as part of the Arts in Your Neighbourhood series.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The March edition is currently taking place in Ang Mo Kio featuring performing arts activities and four new public artworks, on top of its existing visual arts programme.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about Government support for freelancers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In our 2016 Arts and Culture Employment Survey, nearly half of the respondents indicated that they work primarily on a freelance basis.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We agree that more can be done to enhance professional support for independent artists, to help our freelance artists grow meaningful careers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also encourage arts groups and institutions within the wider culture sector to implement these measures.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun spoke about how arts education should involve creative interventions to address societal issues.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I agree that the arts have the potential to do so.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We have, therefore, piloted structured student visits to our arts and heritage institutions over the last two years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to work closely with MOE to help our young develop a stronger appreciation of our history, and our national identity, through the arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: By focusing on positive and enjoyable experiences for our children, we can also develop appreciation for the arts across a lifetime and help us to continue cultivating new artists, audiences and arts champions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On top of our work with students, we have refined our funding support from 2017 to include the promotion of arts accessibility, development of new audiences and building appreciation for the arts across communities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We recognise that these areas may not be an area of priority for all artists and arts groups but will continue to encourage and support those keen to focus on them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I agree with Mr Kok Heng Leun that there is a need for sustainability of the arts sector.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the Cultural Matching Fund and NAC’s efforts to raise fundraising capabilities in the arts sector, we seek to tap multiple sources of support for arts groups and artists.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The ability to raise and manage funding is a critical aspect of sustainable arts groups, regardless of size.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We also agree that our major institutions play an important role and provide a variety of platforms for artists, including those engaged in more experimental work.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that our artists will carry on working in close collaboration with our institutions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Kok Heng Leun and Mr Henry Kwek all spoke on ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our chairmanship of ASEAN this year is an opportunity for us to deepen our appreciation of ASEAN’s rich cultural diversity.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will roll out a series of initiatives to showcase the arts and heritage of our ASEAN neighbours.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, the Asian Civilisations Museum has designated 2018 as the “Year of Southeast Asia” and will feature programmes and exhibitions in line with the theme.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Singapore will also host residencies for artists around the region, just as our neighbours will host ours.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also celebrate the close cultural ties with two ASEAN partners – Malaysia and Indonesia – through bilateral cultural showcases.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These initiatives complement ongoing efforts to support Singapore artists' development through participation in regional and international festivals, trade fairs, biennales and overseas training programmes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: One example of this support is the return exhibition of local artist Zai Kuning's work "Dapunta Hyang: Transmission of Knowledge".

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We were able to preview this piece as a work-in-progress before it represented Singapore at last year's Venice Biennale.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Singaporeans will have the opportunity to view it when TheatreWorks presents it from April.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is a culmination of Zai's ongoing body of work over the years to investigate Malay history and culture, and Singapore’s relationship with the larger Riau Archipelago.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are proud of how our Singapore stories are travelling around the world and remain committed to supporting our artists in such pursuits.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Chairman, youth is another key focus for our ASEAN Chairmanship.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: By 2020, almost half of ASEAN's population will be under 30 years old.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This underscores the importance of empowering our youths to appreciate and realise the potential of ASEAN's youthful demographic in driving the region's future.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Today, MCCY, MOE and our economic agencies provide opportunities for our youths to build a greater appreciation of ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, the National Youth Council hosts bilateral youth leaders' exchange programmes with Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: MOE provides our students opportunities through exchange and immersion programmes, cultural exchanges like the annual Singapore Youth Festival and through sports like the annual ASEAN Schools Games.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: International Enterprise (IE) Singapore runs the Young Talent Programme, an initiative for youths to have international immersion experiences to better prepare them for global careers in future.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The programme has supported Singaporeans to take on overseas internships and hybrid work-and-study programmes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Since last year, this programme has focused on fast-growing Asian markets, including Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I urge our youths to take up these opportunities in the region, as we work with MOE and economic agencies to ensure even greater access to these regional opportunities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Fund supports ground-up initiatives by ASEAN youths in areas, such as leadership development, community service and entrepreneurship.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As a highly popular and trending activity among youths, eSports has tremendous potential as an innovative means of engagement to connect ASEAN youths through shared experiences of competition, sportsmanship and fun.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Take the example of Amos Ker, a professional gamer playing Vainglory, a Massive Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA).

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Amos has bagged numerous regional awards and even competed internationally at Hollywood.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through the various tournaments, Amos has made many friends from different countries and acquired a confidence to lead and share his experience with aspiring competitive gamers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Today, Amos is the captain of Team Impunity, a local eSports team.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: He is also pursuing a Diploma in Game Development, under scholarship at the Informatics Academy.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The ASEAN eSports tournament will be the first of its kind in the region.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It will be part of a larger celebration of our vibrant ASEAN youths during the first weekend of August at the Singapore Sports Hub, bringing together the SHINE Festival for Youths and GetActive!

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our youths at home can look forward to a diverse array of opportunities and performances in eSports, live music, dance and sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I encourage our youths to showcase their talents, represent Singapore on the regional stage, and build new friendships with our ASEAN neighbours.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These ASEAN Youth Fellows will be spending a week together in Singapore in the second half of this year, discussing key issues and opportunities in respective home countries as well as the greater ASEAN region.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Youths of Singapore will also have the opportunity to interact with this next generation of leaders.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond our chairmanship this year, we hope to build a network of ASEAN young leaders to take the ASEAN community forward as a strong and united body.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In addition to ASEAN youth initiatives, MCCY is nurturing our youths to be more confident and resilient.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked for an update on the progress of the MOE-OBS mixed school cohort camps.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: While the design and development of OBS@Coney is underway, MOE and MCCY started phasing in students for the MOE-OBS Challenge Programme in 2017.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Each week, Secondary 3 students from different schools are given the opportunity to team up into expedition groups and interact with peers from different backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Last month, I met with two such participants – Nur Syarafina from Edgefield Secondary School and Andre Loh from Anglo-Chinese School (Independent).

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Both of them were, at first, intimidated by the challenging tasks at OBS, as well as the initial "awkwardness" of working together with peers from other schools and different backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This "awkwardness" soon melted away as the two worked with team members to conquer kayaking expeditions and challenging ropes courses.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They remain in touch with their new friends, and I am told that a group of them even met up over the recent Chinese New Year period.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over the course of 2017, the MOE-OBS Challenge Programme brought together 6,000 youths like Andre and Syarafina from different schools to work together and overcome challenges in the outdoors.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The outcomes from the inaugural programme have been positive thus far, with our youths becoming more confident, resilient and making new friends.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Over 80% of students surveyed are also keen to attend another OBS course.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: About 90% reported better appreciation of diversity and being better at working with peers from different backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will continue to gather feedback from future participants and refine the programme.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Alongside the vibrant arts and youth sectors, our people can be proud of a thriving sporting scene.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our athletes have worked hard in making Singapore a proud sporting nation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Team Singapore broke new grounds in 2017, with excellent results at the 29th SEA Games and 9th ASEAN Para Games in Kuala Lumpur.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Both contingents put in historic away Games performances, bringing home a remarkable 188 and 50 medals respectively.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our young Team Singapore athletes also won a record 18 medals at the 2017 Asian Youth Para Games in Dubai.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our athletes bring the nation together and exemplify the Singapore Spirit – a "can-do" attitude, the relentless pursuit of excellence and the determination to overcome all challenges.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In early 2017, she sustained three hairline cracks in her lower back, putting her out of action for several months.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But she did not let this setback get her down.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: With the help of conditioning coaches, physiotherapists and performance analysts from the National Youth Sports Institute, she made a swift and full recovery in time for the 2017 SEA Games.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: She went on to win Gold in the Sabre event.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is just one of many inspiring stories of our athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We wish them the very best as they continue to train hard and do Singapore proud on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Darryl David asked how we are helping our Team Singapore athletes achieve even greater success.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Government is committed to supporting our athletes' aspirations and will continue to work with stakeholders to ensure that with our High Performance Sports (HPS) system, our athletes can achieve their best.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are working with various NSAs to be more professional in organisational governance and technical expertise.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also continue to enhance areas, such as talent identification and development, coach development through CoachSG, sports science and medicine capability and athlete support systems, in terms of carding, support for Major Games' preparations, scholarships as well as career and education opportunities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is over and above the existing funding for NSAs, carded athletes and spexScholars.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This will give Games-bound athletes greater assurance and encourage more to train fulltime, as they strive for success at these competitions.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To supplement the Government's efforts in improving our HPS system, the One Team Singapore Fund (OTSF) was launched in October last year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Now, Singaporeans can directly contribute to the HPS system by pledging support to this Fund.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We look forward to more donations to OTSF, as efforts to increase awareness of the Fund ramp up this year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Importantly, the Fund also provides impetus for NSAs and Team Singapore athletes to deepen their engagement with their respective fraternities, as well as the wider community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Ganesh Rajaram and Mr Faisal Manap asked about developments in local football.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Specifically, FAS has updated S League match rules to provide younger players with more match exposure.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It has taken steps to raise player professionalism, such as cracking down on smoking and placing more emphasis on fitness.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: FAS is also working on raising coaching standards.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On SportSG's end, the ActiveSG Football Academy is collaborating with FAS to build the youth development system.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As with other NSAs, SportSG will work in partnership with FAS to review its strategic plans for football annually against the funding it receives, to ensure the continued development of Singapore football and the revamped S League.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We note that the football fraternity has responded positively to the plan of FAS.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We expect the FAS leadership to continue engaging and working closely with clubs, stakeholders and fans or, as Mr Manap says, current and ex-footballers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We look forward to improvements in the standard of Singapore football and the performance of our National Teams.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The new S League season kicks off at the National Stadium on 31 March and we wish them all the best.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Chairman, just as teamwork is crucial in sports, it is only by working hand in hand that we can realise our shared goals for Singapore, be it in the arts, youth or sports sectors.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Together, we can be confident of making Singapore our home where we can all lead fulfilling lives and pursue our dreams.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Chairman, I am glad to hear about the dollar-to-dollar matching from the Parliamentary Secretary just now.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I have earlier on suggested in my response speech to the Budget that Singaporeans should be given an easy way to donate their SG Bonus to worthy causes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And some of these causes are associated with matching funds.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Others are not, but we think they are all equally worth promoting.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: We have been working with NAC for only a few months and we are very glad that you have speedily decided to adopt the recommendations.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I have two clarifications that I require from the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: One is whether NAC will also similarly take a leading role in trying to mediate disputes between the freelancers and the buyers of their services so that there is a platform for them to settle payment disputes and issues concerning payment.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: The second question is: apart from NAC, how about venue operators and event organisers that take funds from NAC?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Will the Ministry also require that these operators and venue owners similarly adopt recommendations to safeguard and protect the interests of freelancers that participate and take part in events hosted by the event organisers or the venue operators?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope that with the establishment of the National Resource Centre for freelancers, it could perhaps play a role, and I hope that we can also count on the other national bodies, for example, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management, to resolve such issues.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But we definitely will encourage our vendors to respect freelancers and to also adopt the measures that we have.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I have about six things that I need to clarify.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The first is to either the Senior Minister of State or the Minister.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I was just wondering whether the Senior Minister of State or the Minister would consider approaching the President to support the arts, like what they have in the President's Charity, to create a kind of platform where the President could be the person to champion the arts and get the private as well as corporate donors to come in to support arts through donations.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The other clarifications are more for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: It is good to know that we are pushing more into heritage.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, I also want to know an update on how the Traditional Art Centres would be working within that trajectory?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The Traditional Art Centres, up to this point, would like to know what is the development and how to go along.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The third clarification is on the Public Art Trust.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: It is good that we are designating more places so that we can do the public arts.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I think there is also an issue of the maintenance of the public arts whereby it needs the right people to be there to maintain, it needs funding for it to be maintained, because public arts allow people to do interaction.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: How would NAC be looking at that and working with the various stakeholders?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Next, it is about individual artists as well as artists who are in their mid-career.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: A lot of artists, whether they are in performing arts or in visual arts, sometimes, nowadays, their work tends to span across durations of between one and two years.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Could the Member just pose the clarification and not make a speech?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, I just want to know whether NAC would look at shifting some of its grant system to allow all these arts groups or artists to get grants that cover over two or three years rather than being ad hoc and on a project basis?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Lastly, it is about the "ling ting liu su".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: This one I would have to ask in Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: (In Mandarin):   Hear65 is a very good idea.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: In the early days of Singapore, arts groups and musicians, such as Leong Yoon Pin and Poon Yew Tien, have written many folk songs.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Can these songs be included in Hear65 as well?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: When we talk about Singapore music, we do not want people to only think about pop music in the market.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: In fact, there are rich cultural resources in these arts groups.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These are not meant to be on a permanent basis as permanent art works will require a different set of requirements to maintain and upkeep.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Even though on a temporary basis, we also expect that the art works should be kept in good condition during the duration so that the public can enjoy them and appreciate the talent of our local artists.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This will be a process that we look forward to working together with the artists as well as the venue owners so that we can all learn from the process of creating exciting art works that would excite local audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Kok Heng Leun talked about songs included in Hear65.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Indeed, music on this platform should not only showcase commercial or pop music, but also artistic music which is not so familiar to the public.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through this platform, we hope that Singaporeans can better appreciate the diversity of our local artists and musicians, therefore, further supporting our local music production.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Parliamentary Secretary for his responses on the state of football in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram
text: A year ago, when I made my speech about how bad things were, I think the Parliamentary Secretary's response at that time was that the new council was about to be elected, let us give them some time.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram
text: It has been one year and things have gotten progressively worse.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram
text: So, my question to the Parliamentary Secretary is that, given the status of football today, is SportSG happy with the developments over the last year, and what is the timeframe that it is giving FAS to ensure that standards are raised?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Ganesh Rajaram would be familiar with how the sports fraternity works.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is pretty much driven by the respective NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, in this case, the FAS has its own constitution and management and a new team in place.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: SportSG will have to work with the new team on the new directions, the new focus they have.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And through our funding on specific programmes, like for example, in fitness, in the development of youths, that is where we will work closely with them.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are supportive of their focus on the youths because that is also where the focus is for our regional games, like the SEA Games and Asian Games, where the focus is on the under 22 years old or 23 years old.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We believe that will also translate well for the development of Singapore's football in the long term because that will help us create a very strong pipeline of talent for the senior team.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I just want to remind the Parliamentary Secretary that there was a question about the mid-career artists that has not been answered.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I have one more point that I just thought about.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Just now, fellow Member Mr Ang Hin Kee talked about freelancers.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I also wonder if NAC would come in because there are a lot of freelancers who have been contracted by some intermediaries and these are private vendors.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: A lot of times, they would take advantage of all these freelance artists.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In my earlier response, what NAC and NHB have full control or better control over are the artists that we contract directly.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As for those who are through intermediaries or event organisers, we will definitely influence and encourage them to adopt such standards.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Ultimately, we want our freelancers – they are all very hardworking, talented people – we would want them to have meaningful careers but also, at the same time, financially viable careers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, this is a first step we are doing.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: And we hope that the society at large, all users, procurers of artistic talent and works, will also respect the freelancers' way of business as part of the overall gig economy that Singapore is experiencing together with the world.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, that is something we will work on.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I would like Mr Kok Heng Leun to repeat his question on the mid-career artists.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Mid-career artists sometimes may need grants that go across a certain period of two to three years.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, nowadays, grants are given usually on a project basis over a year.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: That hinders their progress, especially their process of innovation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As long as the work contributes towards the Singapore Arts scene, I cannot see any reason why NAC would have any objection to that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the mover wish to withdraw the amendment?
